0.1.n: This links the name to ございます, forming a very polite version of です.

0.2.n: ござい is the connecting form of ござる; together with で and ます, it makes the introduction very polite.

0.3.n: This ending adds politeness and completes でございます.

1.0.n: This refers to the current video or presentation.

1.1.n: This marks 今回 as the topic: what the speaker will do this time.

1.2.n: This tells us when the speaker stayed at the inns.

1.3.n: Past form of 宿泊する, placed before 温泉旅館 to describe the inns the speaker stayed at.

1.4.n: This describes the type of 旅館: an inn with hot spring baths.

1.5.n: 旅館 refers to Japanese-style accommodation, often featuring traditional rooms and meals.

1.6.n: This connects the inns to 中, forming the idea of being among those inns.

1.7.n: With の and から, this identifies the group from which the speaker selects.

1.8.n: This marks the pool of inns used for the selection.

2.0.n: This emphasizes how good the selected inns were.

2.1.n: Past form of 良い, used before 宿 to describe inns that impressed the speaker.

2.2.n: 宿 is a general word for lodging, referring here to the hot spring inns.

2.3.n: 軒 is the counting word used for houses and establishments such as inns.

2.4.n: This marks the five inns as what the speaker will select and introduce.

2.5.n: The て-form of 厳選する connects careful selection to the following introduction.

2.6.n: ご紹介する humbly describes introducing; してまいります politely signals that the speaker will proceed with it.

3.0.n: This introduces the method used to judge the inns.

3.1.n: This marks the evaluation as the topic of the explanation.

3.2.n: Here 宿 names the lodging itself as one scoring category.

3.4.n: This refers to the meals served at each inn.

3.6.n: Here the inn's bathing facilities form a scoring category.

3.8.n: This focuses on how staff welcome and interact with guests.

4.0.n: Listed separately from 接客, this likely covers guest conveniences and services rather than staff interaction.

4.2.n: This names the cost of staying as a scoring category.

4.4.n: Here this refers to sightseeing opportunities associated with the inn's area.

4.6.n: This English loanword names the inn's setting or position as a category.

4.7.n: This links the preceding list to 8項目, identifying those listed features as the eight categories.

4.8.n: This number modifies 項目 to give the total number of scoring categories.

4.9.n: 項目 means individual entries or aspects; here these are the areas being scored.

4.10.n: This marks the eight categories as what receives scores.

4.11.n: 採点し is a connecting form of 採点する, linking scoring to the ranking described next.

5.0.n: This modifies 得点 to indicate a score combining all categories.

5.1.n: This refers to the points earned through the evaluation.

5.2.n: This marks the overall score as the basis for ranking.

5.3.n: ランク付け combines ランク with 付け; adding する makes it a verb meaning to assign ranks.

5.4.n: しております is a humble, polite version of しています, presenting ranking as the speaker's established practice.

0.tip: でございます is a very polite alternative to です, often used in formal introductions.

1.lit: This time, from among the hot spring inns [I] stayed at this year,
1.tip: 宿泊した comes before 温泉旅館: Japanese puts the description before the noun it describes.

2.lit: [I] will carefully select and introduce five inns that were especially good.
2.tip: 宿5軒 means five inns; 軒 is the counting word for establishments.

3.lit: As for evaluation: accommodation, food, hot spring baths, customer service,
3.tip: The list continues into the next line; は introduces the evaluation as the topic.

4.lit: Services, price, sightseeing, location—[I] score the eight categories, and
4.tip: 採点し connects to the next action, so the sentence continues rather than ending here.

5.tip: で marks the basis for the ranking here, not a place where an action happens.
